page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, delivering 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores across 2 threads per core using an x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning comprises 8.0 GB of DDR5 RAM rated at 7 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries an L3 cache capacity of 480 MB alongside comprehensive hardware instruction support, including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and cryptographic acceleration extensions. No local storage is attached, requiring network-attached storage, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps with no dedicated GPUs present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,110.0 and robust throughput in single-threaded compression tests, reaching 34.08 GB/sec in gzip and 13.94 GB/sec in bzip3. Text processing capabilities also placed in the top tier at 2,789.0 points. Conversely, multi-threaded output reflects its burstable CPU allocation and 4 vCPU ceiling: the stress-ng multi-core benchmark score registered at 4,301.36 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 27.63 GB/sec, placing both in the lower percentile. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 40.9 GB/sec, while overall PassMark memory scores ranked lower.

The c8i-flex.xlarge provides balanced compute capabilities for organizations seeking moderate CPU resources without paying for fixed full-core provisioning or unneeded memory overhead. Its combination of DDR5 memory and advanced instruction sets like AMX allows efficient execution of smaller AI/ML inferencing tasks, achieving 506.14 tokens per second during prompt processing on a 135M model. Given its burstable CPU profile and absence of local disks, this instance is suited for batch processing, CI/CD runners, text processing pipelines, and mid-tier web serving workloads that benefit from high single-core frequency but experience variable compute demands.
